extracted.intended_audience: public administrators, legal practitioners, and members of the public seeking guidance on administrative justice in South Africa
extracted.subtask_description: A summary of legal and policy standards governing administrative action in South Africa, centered on the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act (PAJA) and relevant constitutional principles (Section 33 and 195). Useful for officials, lawyers, and citizens evaluating or producing administrative decisions and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of Administrative Justice Act, 2000 (Act 3 of 2000)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Promotion of Administrative Justice Act (PAJA) is the primary statutory framework governing administrative action and the promotion of administrative justice in South Africa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site lists PAJA as the key legislation; practitioners should apply PAJA's provisions when assessing administrative action, reasons, review, and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations on Fair Administrative Procedures, 2002
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations enacted in 2002 to give effect to fair administrative procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These regulations set out procedural requirements to be followed by administrative bodies; they supplement PAJA and constitutional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft Code of Good Administrative Conduct (v2) (2006)
rubrics_metrics.description: A draft Code of Good Administrative Conduct produced in 2006 proposing standards for administrative behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though a draft, the Code provides example standards and guidance on good administrative practice and conduct that administrators are encouraged to follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAJA Rules: Procedure for judicial review of administrative action (G 32622, RG 9165, GoN 966) (9 October 2009)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules setting out procedural aspects for pursuing judicial review under PAJA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rules govern the process, filing and conduct of judicial review proceedings challenging administrative action under PAJA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Batho Pele White Paper (Notice 1457 of 1997)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Batho Pele White Paper articulates principles for public service delivery and conduct (referenced as relevant policy context).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Batho Pele contains policy principles relevant to administrative performance and service delivery; the site references DPSA resources for further details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 33(1) — Right to just administrative action
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 33(1): 'Everyone has the right to administrative action that is lawful, reasonable and procedurally fair.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This constitutional right is the core standard for evaluating administrative action: legality, reasonableness (substantive fairness), and procedural fairness must all be assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 33(2) — Right to written reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 33(2): 'Everyone whose rights have been adversely affected by administrative action has the right to be given written reasons.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrators must provide written reasons when their action adversely affects rights; this is a specific procedural entitlement under the Constitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 195(1)(a) — Promote and maintain high standard of professional ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: A high standard of professional ethics must be promoted and maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public administration should cultivate and enforce professional ethical standards in conduct and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 195(1)(b) — Promote efficient, economic and effective use of resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Efficient, economic and effective use of resources must be promoted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative decision-making and implementation should seek to use public resources prudently and effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 195(1)(c) — Development-oriented public administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Public administration must be development-oriented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative actions should contribute to social and economic development objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 195(1)(d) — Impartial, fair, equitable and unbiased service delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Services must be provided impartially, fairly, equitably and without bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service delivery and administrative decisions must avoid discrimination and ensure equitable treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 195(1)(e) — Responsiveness and encouragement of public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: People's needs must be responded to, and the public must be encouraged to participate in policy-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrations should be responsive to public needs and provide meaningful opportunities for public participation in policy processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 195(1)(f) — Accountability of public administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Public administration must be accountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrators and institutions must be answerable for their decisions and performance; mechanisms for oversight and remedy are implicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 195(1)(g) — Transparency through timely, accessible and accurate information
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency must be fostered by providing the public with timely, accessible and accurate information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrations should proactively disclose information needed for oversight and participation, and ensure timeliness and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 195(1)(h) — Good human-resource management and career-development practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Good human-resource management and career-development practices, to maximise human potential, must be cultivated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public bodies should implement HR and training practices that develop staff capacity and professionalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 195(1)(i) — Broad representativity and fair personnel practices with redress
rubrics_metrics.description: Public administration must be broadly representative of the South African people, with employment and personnel management practices based on ability, objectivity, fairness, and the need to redress the imbalances of the past to achieve broad representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruitment and personnel policies must balance merit, fairness and affirmative measures to address historical imbalances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 195(2) — Applicability of principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The above principles apply to administration in every sphere of government; organs of state; and public enterprises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These constitutional principles are broadly applicable across all levels and entities of public administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 195(3) — National legislation must ensure promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: National legislation must ensure the promotion of the values and principles listed in subsection (1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative frameworks (like PAJA and related regulations) are required to give effect to the constitutional principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 195(4) — Appointments on policy considerations must be regulated
rubrics_metrics.description: The appointment in public administration of a number of persons on policy considerations is not precluded, but national legislation must regulate these appointments in the public service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While policy appointments are allowed, statutes must set rules to govern them to prevent abuse and ensure accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 195(5) — Legislative differentiation allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislation regulating public administration may differentiate between different sectors, administrations or institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory regimes may be tailored to sectoral or institutional differences where justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 195(6) — Consideration of nature and functions in legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: The nature and functions of different sectors, administrations or institutions of public administration are relevant factors to be taken into account in legislation regulating public administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lawmakers should consider institutional roles and functions when designing regulatory measures for administration.
